page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.64-512 is an enterprise-scale, general-purpose virtual machine shape built on the AMD EPYC 9J45 processor. It features 64 physical cores supporting simultaneous multithreading, providing 128 dedicated vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. The system configuration pairs these compute resources with 512.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

This instance includes no local storage or dedicated graphics hardware, meaning disk persistence and root file systems rely entirely on remote network-attached block volumes. Network configuration provides one complimentary public IPv4 address. Resource density is high, making it suitable for scale-up computing tasks that benefit from large core counts and uniform memory distribution without requiring specialized acceleration hardware.

The 1:4 memory-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated CPU allocation position VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.64-512 for multi-threaded enterprise workloads. Target deployments include large-scale web application clusters, continuous integration and build pipelines, distributed database servers, and batch data processing pipelines where dedicated processing power and generous memory footprints are required.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.64-512 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 64 physical cores across 128 dedicated vCPUs and is equipped with 512.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, contains no bundled local storage, and incorporates no GPU hardware accelerators, directing disk I/O to external cloud block volumes. Designed for high-density compute environments, the server delivers uniform multi-core throughput and sufficient memory capacity for large-scale application tiers, enterprise data processing, relational databases, continuous deployment automation, and batch computing tasks.
